summary: The German Value Investor revisits NN Group, the Dutch insurer he bought at ~€44 (4.4% of his community portfolio), now up 86% plus ~12% in dividends at ~€80, and asks whether it is still a buy. His answer: a hold, fairly valued — he would add under €65 and trim over €86. The bull case rests on shareholder returns: a 5% dividend yield (raised again for H1, targeting ~7% annual payout growth), share buybacks lifted from €300M to €350M per year, and a 224% solvency ratio — well above the 150-200% target corridor, leaving room for special dividends or bigger buybacks. H1 operating result grew 4.4% (he dismisses the +170% net-result jump as investment-portfolio noise typical for insurers); his scenario calculator gives a 2.86/5 quality grade — solid, not great — with adjusted P/E 13.2 and price-to-book ~1.0 versus ~0.6 historically. Scenarios: bear (1% growth, P/E 9.7 in 10y) → fair €62, still +3.4%/yr via the dividend; normal (4% growth) → fair €84, ~7.7%/yr; bull → €91. Risks: a saturated insurance market and below-market return on equity. Analysts: 7 buy, 8 hold, 0 sell of 15, price targets €74–€100. A teaser at the end points to a McDonald's video after its 27% plunge.
title: 86% Gain on a Stock Almost Nobody Knows
